architecture_decisions: Wave 4 preserves the deployed Wave 3 authority model: The durable experience contract explicitly keeps canonical Project/Work Specification/run/source-lineage/worker/tool/provider/evaluation/REVIEW…
work_items: Wave 4 maintains the same design and execution model as Wave 3, ensuring that the product remains consistent with the previous version.
validations: Wave 4 adheres to the same design principles and execution strategy as Wave 3, ensuring that the product remains functional and reliable.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — The durable experience contract explicitly keeps canonical Project/Work Specification/run/source-lineage/worker/tool/provider/evaluation/REVIEW authority server-owned and forbids Live Development/Observability from creating a competing state or mutation path.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — The product contract permits actual stage/action/file/diff/registered-command/test/provider/evaluation/recovery evidence while explicitly rejecting hidden chain-of-thought, scratchpad, raw provider payloads, credentials and unrestricted logs.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — SPECIFY/PLAN/IMPLEMENT/BUILD/TEST/VERIFY/REVIEW presentation, completion state, retries, recovery and stop reasons derive only from persisted runtime facts; fixture/placeholder/loading state cannot masquerade as live successful work.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Follow Live, Pause View, tab selection, scrolling, disconnect and reconnect cannot pause, cancel, resume, advance or duplicate the worker. Protected Pause/Resume/Cancel/REVIEW controls remain distinct server-authorized actions.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Code/diff views are tied to exact immutable source-lineage identities, and terminal/test views consume bounded redacted registered-command evidence. No general filesystem write, shell, command or network surface is authorized.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — The durable design direction specifies dark forest/olive navigation, warm ivory/cream workplane, rust active/action color, flat teal live interaction, restrained olive status/support and charcoal content, with centralized semantic tokens and no silent fallback to the previous dominant violet/cyan theme.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Later client acceptance must preserve the three-region desktop hierarchy, prominent run pipeline, compact KPI row, dominant central event/Live Build workspace, secondary right utility rail and subordinate summary rhythm, with screenshot/browser assertions rather than subjective prose alone.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Phone layouts reflow into focused tabs/drawers/stacked content; touch, text size, zoom, keyboard/visualViewport safety, selectable content, explicit state labels, reduced motion and reduced graphics preserve equivalent capability.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Later telemetry implementation must use stable Project/run-scoped event identity with monotonic per-run ordering, preserve source/attempt/evidence references, resume after process/observer recreation and avoid duplicate accepted event display or duplicate runtime/provider mutation.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Unavailable/degraded telemetry, recoverable execution failures, process recovery, HUMAN_REQUIRED, specification amendment, credential/authority boundaries and REVIEW are visually/textually distinct and cannot be converted into success or generic retry by the client.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Mockup/screenshot similarity is a protected product requirement, but deterministic functional/accessibility/security/runtime evidence remains higher precedence. Visual acceptance may not waive protected failures or production boundaries.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Every implementation workstream remains spec-first with authentic DSPy evidence and exact-head protected gates. Final integrated release requires browser/accessibility/visual proof, migration readiness where applicable, Preview/rollback evidence and deployment verification before `CURRENT-STATE.md` records production; standing single-user release authorization removes only a repeated approval wait.
risks: Wave 4 maintains the same risk and mitigation strategies as Wave 3, ensuring that the product remains secure and compliant with the previous version.

critique: The product contract for the Wave 4 implementation includes a durable experience that is coherent and understandable. It uses a three-region product composition with a dark forest navigation rail, a warm primary workplane, and a warm right utility rail. The product contract specifies that the live development and observability features are one Wave 4 program and are validated together before release. The product contract also specifies that the live development and observability features are not simulated, exposed, or created a generic IDE/shell. The visual target is the user-approved Parallax mockup family from the active autonomous app-builder runtime.
